ABSTRACT: In synthetic chemistry, controlling the regio- and stereoselectivities,
especially nontraditional selectivities, of multicomponent tandem reactions has
always been challenging. In organic reactions, single-atom catalysts (SACs) possess
fixed coordination structures and adjustable metal−support interactions and
frequently generate products possessing well-defined regio- and stereoselectivities.
Herein, a silicon carbide (SiC)-supported copper SAC (CuCl @O−SiC) was
synthesized using increased copper content and the interaction between the metal
support and SiC was regulated through oxygen-based surface modification. Allenes
underwent nontraditional β,γ-addition, exclusively generating Z-configured
alkylboronization products. These findings revealed the β,γ-selectivity pattern in
allene addition reactions, which advances the application of SACs in chemical catalysis. This work ofers the potential for further
developments in selective synthesis.

were conducted using a homogeneous catalytic system;
however, the results were unsatisfactory (Table S1, entries
1−8). To determine the efects of various transition-metal
carbides on the selectivity and catalytic activity of alkyne
hydroboration, a series of metal-carbide-supported Cu-based
SACs was synthesized to evaluate their catalytic activities. The
experimental results revealed that during the reaction, diferent

suggesting that the interaction between the metal support
and catalyst plays a crucial role in modulating the
regioselectivity of the reaction. Evidently, although both the

■ CONCLUSIONS
Overall, the synthesis of complex multisubstituted olefins
presents formidable challenges, particularly in accelerating
reactions, maintaining catalyst stability, and fine-tuning the
reaction stereoselectivity. To overcome these challenges, we
synthesized a SiC-supported copper SAC (CuCl @O−SiC)
containing increased Cu loadings via oxygen-based surface
modification and used the catalyst in the multicomponent
boronization of special β,γ-addition-associated branched
olefins. These findings should advance research on the
synthesis of complex multisubstituted olefins and provide
more possibilities for advances and breakthroughs in synthetic
chemistry.
